recipes.name: Pammy's Slow Cooker Beans
ingredients_raw: 8 cups water, or more if needed

steps.text: Wash and pick over beans; place in a large bowl. Fill with cold water; soak beans 6 to 8 hours.

Drain and rinse beans; place in a slow cooker. Add 8 cups water to the slow cooker; stir in onion, garlic powder, bay leaves, black pepper, and onion powder. Place turkey leg in the slow cooker; cover.
Cook on Low setting for 6 hours. Stir in olive oil, add more water if beans are beginning to dry out; cook until beans are very tender, 2 hours more.

raw_recipe.headline: Pammy's Slow Cooker Beans
raw_recipe.description: Pammy's slow cooker beans recipe yields delicious pinto beans. To amp up the flavor, use smoked turkey leg rather than pork. Serve with rice or cornbread.

review.reviewBody: These beans were good but I altered the recipe a bit. I didn't have a spare smoked turkey laying around so I used chopped leftover ham instead. Tasted great! I also added Paula Deen's House Seasoning to the beans when I added the olive oil. Wasn't sure how the olive oil would taste, but it turned out great. I usually make my beans on the stove top and add vegetable oil. I also cooked the beans on high the whole time which gave me more of a "pot liquor" which I love to sop up with my corn bread. I will surely be making these again. :)

Thank you SO much for a great base bean recipe! The beans turned out perfect for me. I added salt after 6 hours. (I cooked for 9 hours total.) I also used a few slices of bacon rather than the turkey. THIS is the perfect recipe for making beans to add to dishes, or just on it's own!

These are the BEST beans I've EVER EATEN!!!!!! I soaked 2lbs of dried beans overnight, rinsed them and added them to the slow cooker. I also added a large diced onion, a large diced bell pepper, 2 smoked turkey legs, 1 clove of garlic, pepper, a little less than half a tbsp of sea salt, and just under 8 cups of chicken broth. I set the slow cooker on Low for 8 hours. Came home, made a dozen gluten free cornbread muffins and had the BEST home cooked meal I've eaten in a long time!!! I already gave this recipe to my Mother and Grandmother to make too! This recipe is hands down the BEST ever and this will be my signature dish from now on! Thank you for this recipe!!!!!

My husband asked for a pot of beans and this recipe seemed to be closest to what he was asking for. I have never cooked beans because I don't like the gas. But I did some research on how to eliminate it and this recipe covered it. The soaking for at least 8 hrs and rinsing well is important. The other gas eliminating property is the Bay Leaves. My Bay leaves were very small, so I put 2.5 of them in (one was a broken leaf, lol). I have no idea where to get a Smoked Turkey Leg, but I had some Country Ham pieces I had bought for cooking with and used about a third of that package. I also added about 2T of Wyler's Chicken Granules at another reviewers suggestion. I was worried about adding it at the beginning because I had read salt will make the beans tough, but since I had to leave, I went on and added all my ingredients at the beginning except for the Olive Oil. I only had 6 hrs to cook, so I started them on high for 1.5 hrs, then changed to low when I had to leave home. The beans came out great, and not tough. If I had returned home earlier, I may have added the Olive Oil, but decided not too add at the last minute. They were done in time for me to take a meal to my 90 and 93 yr parents who were excited when I told them I would bring them beans for dinner. My 92 yr mother-in-law is getting some leftovers and she will love them too. I served with cornbread. Best part is, NO GAS!!! So I will definitely make sure to not only soak well, but add the Bay Leaves.

I've been using smoked turkey drums instead of pork shanks with my beans for years now. They always taste fantastic. I half the onions and add three leeks, 3 chopped carrots, and 3 stalks celery with tops. I use 4 cans 14.5 oz cans chicken broth instead of water.

I make this quite often. Used a turkey thigh and a turkey leg I got from whole Foods. Cook the beans after soaking them overnight by themselves for five hours then add turkey and cook for another 3 to 4 hours. I add knorr bouillon cubes instead of all of the seasonings mentioned along with pre diced onions for convenience. Turns out great every time

I love this recipe and have made it many times over the years. Sometimes I use ham hocks and sometimes the smoked turkey leg called for in the recipe. Today I’m using fully cooked, bone-in, smocked pork chops that I found in the grocery meat case. The recipe is so simple and always comes out great, no matter what kind of meat I use. Great bean recipe; will be making this again! Only modification was to use two turkey legs, a little ham base and no rice - just ate it as soup. Yum!!

good! I can't wait to make again! I followed recipe almost to the T. But, I used 7 cloves of fresh garlic plus garlic powder. I used 2 smoked hamhocks. No oil and no bay leaves. I also used almost 2Tb chicken bouillon near the end of cooking so I wouldn't over salt it. SOOOO good!!
I used a spiral ham bone in place of smoked turkey wings, crushed red pepper in place of black pepper, and after tasting the beans I added 1 teaspoon of Lawry's seasoned salt to the pot of beans.
This was tasty. I didn't have pinto beans so I used great northern beans and added a touch of poultry seasoning at the end of cooking time. I cooked it 5 hours on high and 3 hours on low.
Excellent recipe, but since I didn't have a turkey leg on hand, I used a ham hock...I'll surely make this one again. Delish!
Used 15 bean instead of red beans, used up leftover smoked turkey.

Changes for personal preference:
-large, very meaty hambone
-1/2 med onion
-1 T minced garlic
-no onion powder
-add salt and pepper
-no oil
I made this, but added chicken broth for more flavor.
Didn’t have smoked turkey leg, so used leftover turkey and a few bacon slices.
I use smoked ham hock instead of turkey.
Wonderful recipe! Best seasoning ever. Thanks for sharing. ..

My beans took a little longer because I didn't put enough water when I soaked them. When the beans were finally finished they were great. I used onion salt instead of onion power. I added a dash of salt for a little more flavor. I will make this recipe again. Thank you.

I give it 4 stars because the recipe as written is very bland. But it's a great starting off point for being creative. The beans cook perfectly and will go well with whatever additions you choose to make.
